scope: Two representative defenses plus benchmark-criticism source; no experiments

sources.title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; no separate venue verified
claim: Provenance signalling through delimiting, datamarking and encoding with matching system instructions.
Keyword-payload ASR and NLP task utility are separate evaluations; input transformations are not enforced action authorization.
limits: 1000 synthetic keyword-payload documents and older GPT-family models; not an agent-specific adaptive security guarantee.
Encoding can impair task utility; delimiters and marking implementation choices affect bypass risk.
No performance percentages copied; no reproduction or code audit.
sources.reading_depth: Metadata and specified sections; no full proof or figure-value audit

sources.title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
sources.version: PMLR final metadata; author arXiv 2502.05174v4, 2025-06-10, selected PDF sections cross-checked; whole-document equality unverified
claim: Masked state retains observations but replaces user task and removes prior actions; original candidate tool calls are compared to cached masked calls by semantic similarity.
Detection occurs after action generation and before execution; positive detection terminates the agent run.
The ensemble error bounds explicitly require mu_B < threshold < mu_V; this is not unconditional deployment security.
Legitimate external-instruction delegation creates false-positive interpretation disputes; response-based attacks and differing tool use can evade the detector.
limits: Requires complete agent-state access and legitimate-user-task assumption.
Similarity representations omit some arguments; no alert is not equivalent to user authorization.
Hoeffding applicability and dependence between same-model masks were not independently validated.
No performance percentages copied; no experimental reproduction.
sources.reading_depth: Official metadata; author HTML targeted sections; official 20-page PDF targeted theoretical and error-analysis sections, no complete equality or proof audit

sources.title: Indirect Prompt Injections: Are Firewalls All You Need, or Stronger Benchmarks?
claim: Benchmark replacement can remove task-critical data; rigid utility checks can conflate task completion and side effects.
Forced attack-tool inclusion and tool-set-only task checks can distort ASR and utility.
Abstract perfect-security wording must be restricted to tested original attacks because the paper reports successful adaptive bypasses.
Revised and original benchmark metrics must not be combined into a cross-paper ranking.
limits: Benchmark implementation claims were read, not independently reproduced.
User trusted and tools secure except poisoned observations are explicit assumptions.
Cascade stages have conditional populations and differing budgets; no performance percentages copied.
LLM sanitization is not deterministic authorization; semantic fidelity and classifier errors need independent testing.
sources.reading_depth: Metadata and sections 3,4.2,7–10,D,E,F; no full table or benchmark-code audit
